newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Russia seeks negotiations towards nuclear disarmament.
newsitem.headline: Russia seeks negotiations towards nuclear disarmament.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov called on Thursday on the Conference on Disarmament to break its impasse and launch negotiations to ban production of bomb-making fissile material as the next step in nuclear disarmament.
In a speech to the 61-member forum, Yevgeny said that Moscow also supported negotiating a global ban on anti-personnel landmines in the Geneva body, but it should probably be a phased ban.
"We share the concern of the international community about their irresponsible use," he said of anti-personnel landmines, blamed for killing 25,000 a year.
"We consider the complete ban on anti-personnel land mines as a goal, the movement towards which should probably consist of a number of agreed time stages," he added.
The United-Nations sponsored body has yet to adopted its formal work programme for 1997 due to a row over priorities.

Non-aligned countries, led by India, are insisting the five declared nuclear weapon states (Britain, China, France, Russia, and the United States) agree to launch talks in Geneva aimed at the total elimination of nuclear weapons by the year 2005.
But the nuclear powers have refused the demand for talks on total disarmament, saying cuts in nuclear stockpiles are being made in a bilateral context between Washington and Moscow.
They argue that the next priority in the nuclear field should be negotiations to halt production of bomb-making fissile material (plutonium and highly-enriched uranium).
"Ensuring continuous dynamic development of the disarmament processes is a historic task," Primakov said. "Any pause in this sphere, especially a protracted one, may entail a set-back.

"As to the immediate tasks faced by the Conference on Disarmament, we believe that in the nuclear sphere they include a ban on production of fissionable materials for nuclear weapons or other nuclear devices.
"We are ready for the prompt beginning of negotiations on this issue here, in the multilateral forum on disarmament."
